correct_orders: Obtain laboratory tests: CBC, Coagulation panel, Lipase, AST, ALT
Administer intravenous fluids and antacids to prevent further bleeding and alkalinize gastric pH
Consult Gastroenterology for endoscopic evaluation and management
should_avoid: Order unneeded X-rays or CT scans at this stage as they may not be diagnostic for upper GI bleeding

rationale.Obtain laboratory tests: To assess for anemia, coagulopathy and liver function which may provide clues to the cause of gastrointestinal bleeding
rationale.Order upper GI endoscopy: As it is the gold standard diagnostic test for upper gastrointestinal bleeding
rationale.Administer intravenous fluids and antaci: To prevent further bleeding and alleviate symptoms
rationale.Consult Gastroenterology: For further evaluation and management of the patient
rationale.Order unneeded X-rays or CT scans: As they may not be diagnostic for upper gastrointestinal bleeding at this stage, and may expose the patient to unnecessary radiation
rationale.Reproductive: Pregnancy test is not necessary in this case as the patient's chief complaint is Hematemesis, not related to reproductive issues.
rationale.Type & Screen / Crossmatch: Not required for upper GI bleed unless there is a risk of bleeding that may lead to surgery or transfusion.
rationale.EKG (Electrocardiogram): Not necessary as the patient's chief complaint is Hematemesis, not related to cardiac issues.
rationale.Fingerstick/Serum glucose: While it could be important in some cases, it is not the priority in this case of upper GI bleed.

physical_exam: Hematemesis — exam tailored to chief complaint on arrival.
Soft, non-distended, no focal peritoneal signs on initial exam.
Alert and oriented unless perfusion or metabolic derangement present.
Warm skin with fever; no purpura on initial survey.
